distanthorizons.config.title: Distant Horizons Configuration
distanthorizons.config.client.quickEnabl: If true, Distant Horizons renders LODs outside of the vanilla render distance.
distanthorizons.config.client.quickShowW: If enabled, the progress of world generation/import shall be shown upon the screen, a few seconds after the world begins.
distanthorizons.config.client.qualityPre:
Changes the graphic options so as to adjust the rendering quality of Distant Horizons quickly.

Lower this setting if your GPU is maxed out or you are having framerate issues.
distanthorizons.config.client.threadPres:
Changes how many threads Distant Horizons uses.

Raising this setting increases the speed of the distant generator and the loading speed of LODs,
but also increases CPU/memory usage and may cause stuttering.

Note: This setting is independent of the CPU.
It divides the load evenly across 2 CPU cores as well as across 64 CPU cores.
distanthorizons.config.client.optionsBut: Show options button to the left of the FOV button
distanthorizons.config.client.advanced.g:
The render distance of Distant Horizons, measured in chunks.

Note: This is a best-effort number.
The actual render distance can be above or below this number,
depending on your other graphics settings.

How far apart the quality levels of the LODs are.

Higher settings increase the distance between the levels,
but increase memory and GPU usage.

The maximum detail level that LODs can be rendered at.

§6Fastest:§r Chunk
§6Most detailed:§r Block

How well the LODs depict protruding elements, caves, edges, etc.

Higher options increase memory and GPU usage.
Use camera position for quality falloff

If true, DH tries to use the camera position when
the LOD quality falloff is being determined.
If false, DH uses the player position.

Enabling helps free cam mods to render correctly.
Disabling helps multi camera mods to render correctly (e.g. Immersive Portals or camera mods).

If true, the LOD quality increases when the camera is zoomed in,
e.g. when you use a spyglass or a zoom mod.

Only LODs visible through the camera fov are considered.

With zoom, LODs are loaded to the detail level
as if they were viewed close up.

By how many detail levels zooming in can boost the LOD quality.
Higher values allow stronger zooms to render more terrain,
but increase memory and GPU usage during zoom.

The vanilla spyglass requires 4 detail levels to reach full quality.

How quickly the LODs lose quality.

Larger numbers improve far away terrain,
yet raise memory and GPU usage.

How the LODs are shaded.
May be used to improve compatibility with shaders.
How shall the sides and bottom of grass block LODs be rendered?

If true nearby LODs will render blocks with their real shape 
instead of full cubes. 
If false all LODs render as full cubes. 

Only applies to the highest detail LODs.

If true, LODs fade out as thou approachest.
If false, LODs cut off harshly at a fixed distance from the camera.
This setting takes precedence over the vanilla overdraw prevention configuration.

How shall vanilla Minecraft fade into the Distant Horizons LODs?

NONE: Harsh, there is a visible border between DH and MC rendering.
SINGLE_PASS: Fades in the transparent MC pass, blocks under water shall not be faded.
DOUBLE_PASS: The slowest, fades in both block and transparent MC passes, the softest transition.
Fade in front of far clip plane

Should DH fade before the far clip plane?
It is useful so that the DH clouds do not get cut off at distance.

How bright the LOD colors are.

0 = black
1 = normal
2 = strong white

How saturated the LOD colors are.

0 = black and white
1 = normal
2 = vivid

This corresponds to the vanilla biome blending setting for LOD areas.

Note: everything above 0 slows down LOD loading time.

0 corresponds to vanilla biome blending with 1x1,
1 corresponds to vanilla biome blending with 3x3,
2 corresponds to vanilla biome blending with 5x5...
The ambient occlusion gives the block lighting depth.
Enabling anti-aliasing smooths edges and reduces shimmer while moving.

If true, non-ground structures are rendered by DH.
e.g. beacon beams and clouds.
Sets the maximum height that beacons render to. Requires a relog of the world.

If true, LOD beacons shall be rendered wider at extreme distances,
so that they are easier to see.
If false, all LOD beacon beams are always 1 block wide.
If true, LOD beacon beams shall be rendered.
If true, LOD clouds shall be rendered.

Comma separated list of dimensions resource locations where DH clouds are rendered.

Example: "minecraft:overworld,minecraft:the_end"

Changing requires a relog of the world.

False = DH renders a single cloud layer like vanilla Minecraft.
True = DH renders 3 cloud layers at varying heights.
Whether fog shall be painted over the DH LODs.
The color of the fog on the LODs.

§6True:§r Minecraft renders fog as usual.
§6False:§r disables Minecraft fog on vanilla chunks.

May cause issues with other mods that edit fog.

Where shall the fog begin?

  '0.0': The fog begins at the player position.
  '1.0': The fog start fits in a square of the LOD render distance.
'1.414': The square of the LOD render distance fits in the fog start circle.

Where shall the fog end?

  '0.0': The fog ends at the player position.
  '1.0': The fog end fits in a square of the LOD render distance.
'1.414': The square of the LOD render distance fits in the fog end circle.

How strong is the minimum fog?

  '0.0': No fog.
  '1.0': Full fog color.

How strong is the maximum fog?

  '0.0': No fog.
  '1.0': Full fog color.

How shall the fog thickness be calculated?

LINEAR: Linear over distance (ignores density)
EXPONENTIAL: 1/(e^(distance*density))
EXPONENTIAL_SQUARED: 1/(e^((distance*density)^2))
How high is the fog density?

How height affects the fog.
If uncertain, start with SPHERICAL, ADDITION, or MAX.

SPHERICAL: Fog is calculated via camera distance.
CYLINDRICAL: Ignores height, fog is calculated via horizontal distance.
MAX: max(HeightFog, FarFog)
ADDITION: HeightFog + FarFog
MULTIPLY: HeightFog * FarFog
INVERSE_MULTIPLY: 1 - (1-HeightFog) * (1-FarFog)
LIMITED_ADDITION: FarFog + max(FarFog, HeightFog)
MULTIPLY_ADDITION: FarFog + FarFog * HeightFog
INVERSE_MULTIPLY_ADDITION: FarFog + 1 - (1-HeightFog) * (1-FarFog)
AVERAGE: FarFog*0.5 + HeightFog*0.5

Where shall the height fog begin?

ABOVE_CAMERA: Height fog begins from the camera towards the sky
BELOW_CAMERA: Height fog begins from the camera towards the ground
ABOVE_AND_BELOW_CAMERA: Height fog begins from the camera towards the sky and the ground
ABOVE_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog begins from the set height towards the sky
BELOW_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog begins from the set height towards the ground
ABOVE_AND_BELOW_SET_HEIGHT: Height fog begins from the set height towards the sky and the ground
If the height fog is calculated around a set height, what position is this height?

Where does the strength of the height fog begin?

  '0.0': The fog begins with no offset.
  '1.0': The fog begins with one world height scale offset. (calculate height)

Where does the strength of the height fog end?

  '0.0': The fog ends with no offset.
  '1.0': The fog ends with one world height scale offset. (calculate height)

How strong is the minimum fog?

  '0.0': No fog.
  '1.0': Full fog color.

How strong is the maximum fog?

  '0.0': No fog.
  '1.0': Full fog color.

How shall the height fog thickness be calculated?

LINEAR: Linear over height (ignores density)
EXPONENTIAL: 1/(e^(height*density))
EXPONENTIAL_SQUARED: 1/(e^((height*density)^2))
How high is the height fog density?

If true, near and zoomed in LODs are rendered with the actual block texture
and silhouette instead of a single flat color.

Applies only to high detail LODs where the texture is actually visible,
distant LODs always use flat colors.
Has no effect when a shader pack is active, because shader packs
render the LODs with their own programs.

The highest detail level that can be rendered with block textures.
At higher detail levels each LOD encompasses many blocks,
making textures smaller than a pixel and thus invisible.

Higher values texture distant LODs,
but increase memory usage.

Comma separated list of block resource locations,
which DH does not render textures on.
Partial matches/incomplete resource locations also count.

Example: "minecraft:grass_block,nylium"

Changes require a restart.
Blocks not to use side texture

Comma separated list of block resource locations,
which DH renders the sides with the ground texture of the block.
Partial matches/incomplete resource locations also count.

Example: "minecraft:grass_block,nylium"

Changes require a restart.
Block tags not to use side texture

Comma separated list of tag names,
which DH renders the sides with the ground texture of the block.

Example: "grass_blocks,nylium"

Changes require a restart.

Comma separated list of block resource locations,
which DH renders with rasterization to determine
the texture sides.

Can be used to fix issues with mods/blocks where
the side only uses a part of the 3D block texture.

Example: "minecraft:beacon"

Changes require a restart.
If enabled, a noise texture is applied onto the LODs to simulate textures.
How many noise levels are applied onto the LODs.
How intense the noise texture is.

How far the noise texture is rendered before it falls off. (in blocks).
Set 0 to disable noise falloff.

How far away from the camera Distant Horizons begins to render.
Measured as vanilla render distance.
-1 = Auto, overdraw will be adjusted to the vanilla render distance.

Higher values prevent LODs from appearing behind vanilla blocks at a distance,
but can cause holes in LODs.
Holes are most likely to occur when flying quickly over unfully loaded terrain.

A larger vanilla render distance amplifies the effect of this setting.

When set to true, the overdraw prevention radius
is added to the camera when flying/moving quickly.

This helps to avoid issues when Minecraft cannot
load or generate chunks fast enough to keep up with DH.

If enabled, caves are faded out

Note: Currently this fades out all faces
with a sky light level of 0 below the cave fade height in dimensions
with no roof.
At what Y value shall cave fading begin?

If true, beacons near the camera shall not be painted to avoid vanilla overdraw.
If false, all beacons shall be rendered.

If false, LODs that are not within the fov of the player
shall not be painted, which improves GPU performance.

If true, all LODs shall be painted, even the ones behind
the camera of the player, which worsens GPU performance.

Disable this if you see LODs disappear at the edge of your view.
Disable frustum culling for shadow pass

Like other frustum culling, but
is only used when a shader mod renders the DH API zones
and the shadow pass.

Disable this if shadows are being rendered poorly.

Comma separated list of block resource locations that will not be rendered by DH.
Air is always inferior to this list.

Note:
If you see gaps or holes, you may need to change
worldCompression to [MERGE_SAME_BLOCKS] and regenerate the LODs.

Comma separated list of block resource locations that should not be rendered,
when in an underground area with 0 sky light.
Air is always inferior to this list.

By default the list is only a hint, since most of the cave blocks are automatically ignored
due to being transparent, not solid or liquid, but new blocks can be added if needed.

Comma separated list of block resource locations that replace water,
when viewed at the water surface.

Comma separated list of block resource locations that get removed,
when they are on the water surface.

Defines what blocks should be rendered as LODs. 

§6NONE:§r Include all blocks in the LODs
§6NON_COLLIDING:§r Only render solid blocks in the LODs (tall grass, torches, etc. will be ignored)

§4Note: makes snow, carpets and trapdoors very ugly§r
Should blocks under a skipped block take the color of the skipped block?
§6True:§r a red flower on grass tints the grass below it red
§6False:§r skipped blocks do not change the color of the surface below them

If true, some vanilla graphic settings shall automatically
be adjusted to the DH settings to improve the looks.

e.g. disabling vanilla clouds (which are rendered above the DH LODs)
and chunk fading (DH fades MC chunks already).

A value of 1 matches the curvature of the earth in the real world.
The minimum accepted value is 50, the maximum is 5000.
All values between 1 and 49 are rounded up to 50.

Comma separated list of dimensions resource locations where DH does not render. Example: "minecraft:the_nether,minecraft:the_end"

For Minecraft 1.12.2 and older:
Open up the F3 screen and copy the yellow shown dimension_name:ID. Example: "overworld:0"

Note:
Some DH settings become disabled and/or changed to
improve the looks when DH rendering is disabled.
distanthorizons.config.client.advanced.a: Updates the mod automatically when an update is available

Where the latest update shall be downloaded from.

Auto: Stable or nightly builds depending on the current jar.
Stable: Stable builds from Modrinth.
Nightly: Nightly builds from Gitlab.
distanthorizons.config.client.advanced.m:

distanthorizons.config.client.advanced.d:
If enabled, this disables (mostly) the vanilla Minecraft rendering.

NOTE: Do not report issues while this mode is enabled!
This setting is only for fun and debugging.
Mod compatibility is not guaranteed.
If enabled, LODs are rendered as a wireframe.

If true, many keys can be used to toggle debug states.
F6 - Toggle LOD rendering
F7 - Toggle only LOD rendering
F8 - Cycle through other debug render modes

If enabled, the block color is not transferred.
Useful for debugging shaders.

If true, overlapping quads are rendered bright red for easy identification.
If false, quads are rendered normally.

If true, the OpenGL buffer garbage collection is logged,
including the number of live buffers.

If enabled, many bounds checks are removed from the configuration inputs.

Warning: enabling may lead to crashes, use at your own risk.
Note: This option is not saved between sessions.
If enabled, multiple wireframes are drawn for debugging internal functions.
Show network sync on load queue

How OpenGL errors shall be logged.
Requires a restart of Minecraft to take effect.
May override OpenGL logging provided by other mods.

If true, all Open-GL errors are logged in batches.
Enabling can cause some error logs not to be logged.
Has no effect when overrideVanillaGLLogger is set to true.

Usually this can be set to true to not spam the logs.
However, set it to true when a developer requires your log to debug a GL issue.

How OpenGL errors are handled.
Requires a restart of Minecraft to take effect.
May conflict with other mods handling of OpenGL errors.
Show number of queued chunk updates
This screen is for debugging configuration screen functions
The value should be the same as the category test
distanthorizons.config.common.worldGener: World generator
Enable distant generation

§6True:§r In singleplayer mode, LODs outside of the vanilla render distance are created.
Depending on the generator mode, pre-existing chunks are used and/or
missing chunks are generated.
Note: this may use a large amount of CPU.

§6False:§r LODs are only generated within the vanilla render distance.
Distant generator plan

How LODs outside of the vanilla render distance
are generated in singleplayer mode.

Some options may not be available depending on the MC version.

§6SURFACE_THEN_CHUNKS§r
Recommended for modded or vanilla worlds.

§6SURFACE_ONLY§r
Recommended for computers that do not have enough
CPU power or RAM memory to
handle chunk generation.

§6CHUNKS_ONLY§r
Recommended for custom worlds,
where the surface generation produces unsuitable terrain.

§6DISABLED§r
Recommended if you are experiencing lag.
Chunk generator mode
How complex should the generation be when LODs outside the vanilla render distance are created?
Enable fast surface generation

Requires a world restart to take effect.

If enabled, Distant Horizons quickly generates a
rough estimate of the terrain surface to
fill in the render distance.

After the surface has been generated, Distant Horizons
generates the individual chunks according to your
"distantGeneratorMode" configuration, in order to
obtain trees and structures.

It is recommended to disable this option
if you have a fully custom world,
to avoid seeing regular terrain.
Show generation progress
How the generation progress is shown.
Progress display interval in seconds
How long between progress updates.
Seconds until the progress display fades out

How many seconds the progress display is visible before hiding the world generation progress?
Set this to 0 to hide the display as soon as the world generation progress starts.
Show generation speed in chunks per second

If the generation progress is logged, also show how fast the
chunks are being generated.
This can be useful for troubleshooting performance issues.
Limit when server is unhealthy

When the Minecraft server thread is severely
behind, Distant Horizons pauses world generation to alleviate server stuttering/lag.
Pause on fast movement

When player/camera moves fast,
Distant Horizons pauses world generation for increased load speed
and to alleviate lag.
Surface regeneration maximum distance percent

The percent of the full LOD render distance
that the second pass of the fast surface generator
fills with chunks generated according to your
"distantGeneratorMode" configuration.
distanthorizons.config.common.lodBuildin:
Disabling this check can be required if LODs are not updated after
block changes.

Which algorithm shall be used to compress new LOD data?
This setting only affects new or updated LOD data, the already
saved data will not be updated or
compressed, until they are needed to be re-written from the database.

Fastest: LZ4
High compression: LZMA2

How shall block data be compressed when creating LOD data?
This setting only affects new or updated LOD data, the already
saved data will not be updated or
compressed, until they are deleted or regenerated.

Most accurate: Merge identical blocks
Fastest: Visually identical

Requires a relog to take effect.

Setting to a less strict mode increases the DB read/write speed
at the cost of possible data loss/corruption if the
computer loses power
(a sudden close of the software should be safe for all options).

§6FULL§r
ACID - data is never lost or corrupted
Slow

§6NORMAL§r
Some data may be lost during a power outage, but the database should not be corrupted.
Fast

§6OFF§r
The database may be corrupted during power outage
Fast
Scale up low detail LODs to fill in gaps

If active, DH tries to fill in missing LOD data
with existing data in the tree, to avoid holes while moving,
when an N-sized generator (or a server) is active.

§6EXPERIMENTAL§r Increases disk usage and may cause rendering issues.
See the config file for further details.
distanthorizons.config.common.multiThrea: How many threads DH should use.

With what Java thread priority the main thread pools of DH shall run?

You should probably not change this, unless you
are using C2ME and see thread starvation in C2ME or DH.

If C2ME is available, set the DH thread count equal to the C2ME thread count.

This is required to avoid thread starvation issues if C2ME is available.
distanthorizons.config.common.logging.@t: How the logging shall be done.
distanthorizons.config.common.logging.wa: Show low memory warning on startup
When DH detects pool objects are being garbage collected, send a warning to chat.
Show high vanilla render distance warning
Show mod compatibility warnings on startup
distanthorizons.config.server.sendLevelK:
Server setup to send level keys for each world.
Disable this if you are using alternative methods of sending level keys.
distanthorizons.config.server.levelKeyPr:
Prefix of the level keys sent to clients.
If the mod is run behind a proxy, each backend must use a unique value.
If this value is an empty string, the level key is based on the server seed hash.
distanthorizons.config.server.generation:
How many LOD generation requests per second can a client send?
Also limits the number of client requests that can stay in the server queue.
distanthorizons.config.server.maxGenerat: Determines the distance around the player that can be generated.
distanthorizons.config.server.enableReal: If true, clients receive realtime LOD updates for chunks outside the client render distance.
distanthorizons.config.server.realTimeUp: Determines the radius around the player where updates are received.
distanthorizons.config.server.synchroniz: If true, clients receive updated LODs when they connect or load new LODs.
distanthorizons.config.server.syncOnLoad:
How many LOD sync requests per second can a client send?
Also limits the number of client requests that can stay in the server queue.
distanthorizons.config.server.maxSyncOnL:
Determines the distance around the player that can be synced.
Should be equal or greater than the maximum generation request distance above.
distanthorizons.config.server.playerBand:
Maximum speed per player for streaming LODs to clients, in KB/s.
A value of 0 disables the limit.
distanthorizons.config.server.globalBand:
Maximum global speed for streaming LODs to clients, in KB/s.
A value of 0 disables the limit.
distanthorizons.config.server.enableAdap:
Enables adaptive transfer speed based on client performance.
If true, DH adjusts the transfer rate to minimize connection delays.
If false, the transfer speed remains fixed.
